v: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
And immediately in the morning, having made counsel, the chief priests with the elders and scribes and the entire Sanhedrin, having bound Jesus, led {him} away and handed {him} over to Pilate.

As soon as it was morning, the entire Jewish council, including the ruling priests, the other Jewish leaders, and the teachers of the Jewish law, planned {what to do with Jesus}. They had their guards tie Jesus up and take him from there to Pilate{, the Roman local ruler}. They wanted Pilate to condemn him.
the teachers of the Jewish law
They wanted Pilate to condemn him
So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews? “You have said so, Jesus replied.
And Pilate questioned him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” But he, answering him, says, “You say {it}.”
Pilate asked Jesus, “Do you claim to be king over the Jewish people?” Jesus replied, “What you are calling me is right.”
What you are calling me is right
What you are calling me is right
And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.
And the chief priests were accusing him of many things. \*
Then the ruling priests claimed that Jesus had done many bad things. \*
Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!
Now Pilate again was questioning him, saying, “Do you not answer anything? See how many things they are accusing you!”
After that, Pilate again spoke to Jesus. He said, “Listen to all the bad things they claim that you have done! Are you going to reply?”
But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply.
But Jesus no longer answered anything, so as to amaze Pilate. \*
However, Jesus did not respond anymore. How Jesus was acting greatly impressed Pilate. \*
Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
Now at the festival, he was releasing to them one prisoner whom they were requesting.
It is important to know that during the festival period, Pilate usually set free one person who was in jail. {He set free} whomever the people who were in the city of Jerusalem chose.

the people who were in the city of Jerusalem chose
And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
Now there was the one called Barabbas, having been bound with the rebels, who had committed murder in the insurrection.

It is also important to know that a man whose name was Barabbas was in jail with some other men who had rebelled against the Roman government. While they were rebelling, they had murdered some people.
It is also important to know that
some other men who had rebelled against the Roman government
So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
And having come up, the crowd began to request just as he was doing for them. \*
The large group of people {who were there} approached Pilate. They started to ask him {to set someone free}, as he usually did for them. \*
“Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews? Pilate asked.
And Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want {that} I would release to you the King of the Jews?”
Pilate replied, “Would you like for me to set free for you the man who claims to be king over you Jewish people?”
the man who claims to be king
the man who claims to be king
For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over because of envy.
{Pilate asked that question} because he realized that the ruling priests had arrested Jesus and brought him to Pilate because they were jealous {of Jesus}.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd so that he would release Barabbas to them instead. \*
However, the ruling priests convinced the large group of people {to ask} Pilate to free Barabbas rather than {Jesus}. \*
So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?
And Pilate, answering again, was saying to them, “What therefore should I do {with the one} you call the King of the Jews?”
Then Pilate again replied, “So what do you want me to do with the person whom you claim is king over you Jewish people?”
do you want me to do
But they cried out again, “Crucify him!” \*
The large group of people shouted, “{Have your soldiers} kill him by nailing him to a cross!” \*
“Why? asked Pilate. “What evil has He done? But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!
But Pilate was saying to them, “For what evil did he do?” But they cried out even more, “Crucify him.”
Pilate replied, “But he has not done anything wrong!” However, they shouted even louder, “{Have your soldiers} kill him by nailing him to a cross!”
And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
Now Pilate, wanting to do {what} was pleasing to the crowd, released Barabbas to them and handed Jesus over, having flogged {him}, so that he might be crucified. \*
Pilate decided to do what the large group of people wanted. So, he set Barabbas free. Then, he had his soldiers whip Jesus and take him away to kill him by nailing him to a cross. \*
he had his soldiers whip Jesus
kill him by nailing him to a cross
Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.
Now the soldiers led him inside the courtyard (that is, the Praetorium) and call together the whole cohort
After that, Pilate’s soldiers took Jesus into the area just outside {Pilate’s palace}. That place was their headquarters. They summoned the rest of the soldiers who were there.
They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
and put on him a purple robe and place on him, having woven {it} together, a crown of thorns,
They clothed Jesus with a purple robe{, the kind that kings wear}. Also, they took some branches with thorns and laced them together to make a crown. They put it on Jesus’ head.

And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!
and they began to greet him: “Rejoice, King of the Jews!” \*
Then the soldiers started {to mock him by} saying hello to him. They said, “Greetings, you who claim to be king over the Jewish people!” \*

They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.
And they were striking his head with a reed and spitting on him, and bending the knee, they were bowing down to him.
They kept hitting Jesus’ head with a staff. They kept spitting on Jesus {to insult him}. They bowed down in front of him {to pretend} to honor him.
They bowed down in front of him

After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
And when they had mocked him, they took the purple robe off him and put his robes on him and lead him out so that they might crucify him.

After the soldiers made fun of Jesus, they pulled the purple robe off of him. They put his own clothes back on him. Then, some of the soldiers took him {from there to the place where} they were going to kill him by nailing him to a cross.
Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
And they press into service a certain passerby, Simon, a Cyrenean (the father of Alexander and Rufus), coming from the country, so that he might carry his cross. \*

Meanwhile, a man was walking nearby. He had left the farm areas {and was entering the city of Jerusalem}. He was from the city of Cyrene, and his name was Simon. His sons were Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers forced this man to carry the cross for Jesus. \*
He was from the city of Cyrene
They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
And they bring him to the place Golgotha, which is translated, “Place of a Skull.”
The soldiers took Jesus to a place {that people called} Golgotha. That name means “Skull Place.”
There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
And they were giving to him wine having been mixed with myrrh, but he did not receive {it}.
The soldiers offered Jesus wine into which they had mixed a resin that people called “myrrh.” However, Jesus refused to drink it.
into which they had mixed a resin that people called
And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
And having crucified him, also they divide his garments, casting a lot for them, who would take what. \*
After nailing Jesus to the cross, the soldiers split up his clothes by gambling for them. They did that to determine which piece of clothing each soldier would get. \*
They did that to determine which piece of clothing
It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
It was nine o’clock in the morning when they nailed Jesus to the cross.
nine o clock in the morning
nine o clock in the morning
And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And this was the inscription of his charge, having been written: “The King of the Jews.”
The soldiers wrote on a sign why {they were executing Jesus}. Here is what they wrote: “The king over the Jewish people.”
The soldiers wrote on a sign
The soldiers wrote on a sign
Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
And they crucify two robbers with him, one at his right and one at his left.
The soldiers also nailed two bandits to crosses near Jesus. They put one bandit on one side of Jesus and the other bandit on the other side of Jesus.
And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
And the ones passing by were blaspheming him, wagging their heads and saying, “Aha! The one destroying the temple and rebuilding {it} in three days,
The people who walked past Jesus insulted him by shaking their heads {at him}. They said {to him}, “Ha! You said that you could tear down God’s temple and construct it again within three days.

You who are going to destroy

come down from the cross and save Yourself!
save yourself, having come down from the cross!” \*
So, rescue yourself by getting down from that cross!” \*
In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
Likewise also the chief priests, mocking {him} to each other with the scribes, were saying, “He saved others; he is not able to save himself.
Similarly, the ruling priests and the teachers of the Jewish law made fun of Jesus among themselves. They declared, “He has rescued other people. However, he cannot rescue himself!
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe! And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross so that we might see and might believe,” and the ones having been crucified with him were reviling him. \*

{He claims to be} the Messiah and the king over the people of Israel. So, he should get down now from that cross! That way, when we watch {him do that}, we will accept what he says.” The two men whom the soldiers had nailed to crosses near Jesus also insulted him. \*
we will accept what he says
The two men whom the soldiers had nailed to crosses
The two men whom the soldiers had nailed to crosses
From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
And the sixth hour having come, darkness happened over the whole land until the ninth hour.
When it was noon, it became dark in that whole area. {It stayed dark} until three o’clock in the afternoon.
three o clock in the afternoon
three o clock in the afternoon
At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani? which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
And at the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which is translated, “My God, my God, why did you forsake me?”
At three o’clock in the afternoon, Jesus shouted, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” That means, “My God, my God, why did you abandon me?”
At three o clock in the afternoon
At three o clock in the afternoon
At three o clock in the afternoon
When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.
And some of the ones having stood by, having heard {it}, were saying, “Behold, he calls Elijah.” \*
Some people who were there heard {what Jesus said and misunderstood it}. They declared, “Listen! He is speaking to the prophet Elijah!” \*
And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.
And someone, having run and having filled a sponge with vinegar, having put {it} around a reed, was giving {it} to him to drink, saying, “Leave {him}! Let us see if Elijah comes to take him down!”

Then one man quickly went to soak a sponge in sour wine. He attached the sponge to the top of a staff. Then, he held it up to Jesus so that Jesus could suck {the sour wine} from it. Then the man said, “Do not do anything else for him! We should wait to find out whether Elijah appears to help him get down.”
and held it up for [Jesus] to drink

But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
And Jesus, having let out a loud voice, expired.
After that, Jesus shouted loudly. Then he stopped breathing and he died.
Then he stopped breathing and he died
And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
And the curtain of the temple was split in two from top to bottom. \*
And then the drape hanging {in front of the Most Holy Place} in the temple ripped in half; it tore from the top to the bottom. \*
When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!
Now the centurion, having stood by opposite him, having seen that he expired in this way, said, “Truly this man was a Son of God.”
There was a Roman officer standing there in front of Jesus. He observed how Jesus stopped breathing and died. He exclaimed, “This man really was God’s Son!”
And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom {were} also Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the little and of Joses and Salome,

{While all that was happening,} some women were there. They observed {what was happening} from farther away. These women included Salome, Mary from the town of Magdala, and Mary who was the mother of young James and Joses.
These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.
who, when he was in Galilee, were following him and serving him, and many other {women} who had come up with him to Jerusalem. \*

When Jesus was in the region of Galilee, these women had gone with him as his apprentices and had taken care of him. Additionally, many other women were there {observing what was happening}. They had walked to the city of Jerusalem with Jesus. \*
Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath),
And evening already having come, because it was the Day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath,

Now there was a man from the city of Arimathea whose name was Joseph. He was a member of the Jewish council, and people respected him. He too was eagerly expecting God’s kingdom. When he arrived {in the city of Jerusalem}, it was Preparation Day, the day before the Jewish day of rest, and the evening had already begun. Because {it was Preparation Day}, this man went boldly to Pilate. He asked Pilate to allow him to take Jesus’ body {to bury it}.
the day before the Jewish day of rest
Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
Joseph, the one from Arimathea, a respected member of the council who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, having come, having dared, entered in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.
But Pilate marveled if he had already died, and having called the centurion, he questioned him, whether he had already died. \*
When Pilate heard that Jesus might already be dead, it surprised him. So, he summoned the Roman officer {who was in charge of executing Jesus}. Pilate asked the officer, “Is Jesus already dead?” \*
When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
And having learned from the centurion, he gave the corpse to Joseph.
When the officer told Pilate {that Jesus was certainly dead}, Pilate {had his soldiers} give Jesus’ body to Joseph.

So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.

And having bought a linen cloth, having taken him down, he wrapped {him} in the linen cloth and put him in a tomb, which was having been cut from rock. And he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

So, Joseph purchased a fresh sheet of cloth. Then, he removed Jesus’ body {from the cross}. He {prepared to bury it by} winding the fresh sheet of cloth around it. Then, Joseph put Jesus’ body into a grave that Joseph’s workers had made by digging into a rock cliff. After that, Joseph rolled a flat stone to block the entrance to the grave.
Joseph s workers had made by digging
Joseph s workers had made by digging
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.
Now Mary Magdalene and Mary the {mother} of Joses were watching where he had been put. \*
{While that was happening,} Mary from the town of Magdala and Mary who was the mother of Joses observed where Joseph had placed Jesus’ body. \*
